root_idea.summary: The root centers on the continuance, persistence, and firmness of something: what remains in place, endures, or becomes established.
root_idea.development: From remaining and being firm, the root develops meanings of steadfastness, making something firm, establishing or confirming it, and—by extension—immobilizing or securing it. Related derived usages include deliberate verification and seeking confirmation.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form ثَبَتَ.
Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form ثَبَّتَ.
Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَثْبَتَ.
Displayed as the verbal noun تَثْبِيت.
Displayed as the active participle ثَابِت.

senses.definition: To be firm or stand fast.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is an imperative exhortation to remain firm when encountering an opposing force.

senses.definition: To make firm, strengthen, or render steadfast.
senses.usage_conditions: Used causatively of strengthening people, resolve, conviction, or the effective results of action; the Quranic discussions include strengthening believers and making knowledge or deeds more firmly established.

senses.definition: To immobilize, confine, or hinder someone so that he cannot proceed or move freely.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction concerning the plot against the Prophet, the verb is explained as confining him, rendering him unable to rise, and hindering or perplexing him.

senses.definition: To establish, affirm, or confirm something as valid or existent.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the establishing or confirming sense, distinct from rendering a person immobile.

senses.definition: Strengthening, making firm, or securing steadfastness.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic discussions, this includes strengthening conviction by compelling proofs and making knowledge, conduct, or the fruits of action more firmly established.
Used of something firmly rooted or established; the Quranic occurrences describe the firmly established word.

senses.definition: Remaining fixed; firm establishment or stability.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence describes something being firmly planted or established.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stand or become established as a fact or truth; to prove sound, valid, real, certain, true, or correct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A truth, claim, or matter may be described as established or verified.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain, dwell, or abide in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a place as the location in which one remains.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of locusts, to stick their tails into the ground in order to lay their eggs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of the locusts' action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hold fast or persist in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى to express continuing firmly with a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain or become permanent, especially of a case, state, or condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes an idiomatic use wishing that someone's condition remain lasting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become binding, obligatory, incumbent, or due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an obligation, debt, duty, sentence, or entitlement becoming established for or against someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To belong or appertain as an attribute, quality, or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used to express that a characteristic is affirmable or predicable of someone or something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be firm-minded, self-controlled, and steady in understanding, speech, or combat; to be courageous and seldom to err.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a person or horseman who is firm of heart in war or earnest in the charge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hinder, withhold, or prevent someone from carrying out an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَنِ to express holding someone back from an action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vying with another in firmness or steadiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional noun for reciprocal or competitive steadfastness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a spear penetrate a body so that part remains within while its extremity protrudes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction describing the result of a thrust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone fast with a bond, ligature, or other restraint.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Distinct from merely establishing a matter: the object is physically secured.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ascertain, recognize, or verify something with certainty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes knowing a person or thing surely and verifying its true state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To write, register, or record a person's name in a register.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of entering a name in a register of soldiers, pensioners, or accounts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or declare something binding, obligatory, incumbent, or due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of imposing an obligation or making a sentence take effect upon someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affirm or predicate an attribute, quality, or property of someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is asserted to possess the stated characteristic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To authorize a word, signification, or expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage concerning the authorization or acceptance of an expression or meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep fast to someone, scarcely leaving him; of illness, to cling to or remain with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe either persistent attachment or a malady that does not leave the sufferer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To proceed deliberately and without haste; in an affair, to investigate or seek information before acting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with an affair, opinion, judgment, or counsel; the careful investigation sense is included with the deliberate-procedure sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or demand confirmation, evidence, proof, verification, assurance, or certain information; to assure oneself of the true state of a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes seeking an affirmation and checking that something is sound or correct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone firm of heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is reported as an alternative usage; its immediate transitivity is expressly treated as disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person firm or steady of heart, deliberate in conduct, courageous in combat, intelligent, and self-controlled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe one who does not leave his station, is firm-footed in contention, or whose speech does not slip in disputes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firmness or steadiness of heart in war, especially during a charge or at the point of death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for courage and composure in a perilous encounter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Proof, evidence, or a voucher.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as the ground on which a judgment or assertion is made.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An authoritative, trustworthy, just, and exact witness or relater.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person whose reliability makes him evidence for what he relates.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An index or table in which a transmitter of traditions lists what he related and his authorities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical usage associated with tradition transmitters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Continuance, permanence, endurance, stability, firmness, or establishedness; also soundness, validity, certainty, or truth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal expression covering persistence in a fixed state and the resulting established or certain status of a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease that renders a person unable to move.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized, figurative description of immobilizing illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A binding strap, thong, or tie, including the ties of a face veil and the strap used to bind a camel's saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct noun from the stability-related forms, despite the related root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firm in intellect, understanding, strength, or heart, especially in war.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of mental or martial steadiness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, sharp, light, or active in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Continuing, dwelling, or remaining in a place, or lasting for a long time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is used of abiding persons or things, fixed stars, and years that last long.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bound or secured with the strap or thong called ثِبَات.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to something fastened to a camel's saddle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Motionless or bedridden because of illness, a wound, old age, or another disabling cause.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes one who cannot move or does not leave the bed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affirmed or affirmative, as opposed to denied or negated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an affirmative sentence or statement.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The continuance, firmness, and fixed-establishment branches are represented in the Quranic senses; the established-truth branch is separately represented.
Being an attribute or property of someone or something.
Firmness of intellect, self-control, speech, or combat.
Hindering or preventing from an affair.
Causatively making something continue, firm, established, or valid.
Making a spear penetrate and remain partly within.
Making someone fast with a bond.
Quran-attested confining or immobilizing construction and related wound usage.
Persistent attachment or illness that does not leave.
Seeking confirmation, proof, or certain information.
Assuring oneself of the true state of a matter.
Reported firm-hearted meaning retained with its usage qualification.
Firm, deliberate, courageous, and self-controlled person.
Technical index of transmitted traditions and authorities.
Tie or strap of a face veil.
Firmness in intellect, strength, or war.
General active-participle sense is covered by the Quranic firm and established sense.
Abiding or dwelling in a place.
Fixed stars are included in the durable or fixed use.
Motionless through illness, wound, or age.

cautions: Form I is displayed under the normalized perfect citation form ثَبَتَ even though the supplied Quran occurrence is an imperative form.
The Form IV Quran occurrences exhibit two materially distinct uses—immobilizing or confining and establishing or confirming—and these are kept as separate senses.
The reported Form X meaning 'to make firm of heart' is retained as a qualified classical usage because the supplied evidence records a dispute about its immediate transitivity.
